verdict.scope: The generalized whole-lake feature, including its connected southeastern Island Arm.
verdict.formal_authority_note: FWS official usage and published cartography support identity. No current GNIS/BGN naming record was inspected; no claim of a formal current naming adjudication is made.

geometry_integrity.hash_serialization: UTF-8 compact JSON, sorted keys, ensure_ascii=False, matching geometry-reference.json.

spatial_identity_check.method: Complete 104-coordinate polygon rendered and visually compared with the original whole-lake FWS map and separate BLM-hosted northern topo excerpt; not centroid-nearest or name-only matching.
observations: The source outline has a wide northwest-to-southeast main basin and a long narrow southward arm at its eastern end; both components correspond to the labeled lake configuration on the official map.
The source northern basin reaches just north of 58 N between 157 W and 156 W; the independently read Naknek excerpt places the named northern shore in that interval.

The east-side indentation and projecting land between the main basin and southeast arm correspond qualitatively to the mapped peninsula. The FWS text explicitly links Severson Peninsula, Island Arm and the lake.
Source polygon has no interior holes, while the map shows islands. Those land islands are necessarily filled in this generalized polygon; this is not an island-exact water mask.

Southern coastline detail, small embayments, channels and local land edges are generalized. No per-vertex shoreline, land-inclusion percentage, geodetic overlay residual, or survey accuracy is established.
spatial_identity_check.coordinate_anchor_note: These are exact source vertices, not coordinates supplied or independently surveyed by the official publications.
spatial_identity_check.composite_caveat: Visual whole-feature inspection supports a single lake with an internal arm. This is not a precision proof that every generalized pixel excludes neighboring land or connected channels.
